concept.name: Automatic rally
concept.definition: The Wyckoff event (AR) in which price rebounds sharply after a selling climax because intense selling pressure has been exhausted, fueled by institutional demand and short covering. Its high helps define the upper boundary of the accumulation trading range.
concept.intuition: Once the panic sellers are done, even modest buying pops the price back up, like a beach ball released underwater.
concept.mechanics: After the selling climax absorbs panicky public selling, the near-absence of offers lets price rise quickly; the AR high, together with the lows of the selling climax and secondary test, sets the boundaries of the trading range that the analyst uses for subsequent labeling.
concept.failure_modes: The rally is 'automatic' and can fade quickly; its high is not necessarily durable resistance, and in a continuing bear market the AR can be followed by new lows rather than a trading range.
concept.misconceptions: The automatic rally is not yet evidence of a new uptrend; it reflects exhaustion of sellers more than the arrival of committed buyers.
concept.example: After a panic low at 90 on huge volume, a stock bounces to 102 within days on much lighter selling; the analyst draws the top of the developing accumulation range near 102.

citations.source: The Wyckoff Method: A Tutorial (StockCharts.com ChartSchool, by Roman Bogomazov and Michael Lipsett)
